SCHEMA_FEEDBACK_RESPONSE:
- ChatGPT_F004: WITHDRAW. Prior-round item failed all admissibility gates and had an invalid residual-risk computation (`R_k=4603.00`, outside probability bounds). I am not resubmitting it unchanged.

VERDICTS:

CONFIRM C0027 | Evidence: current code uses `re.search(...)` and `break` after the first matching status for each gate. Concrete input:
```text
ADMISSIBILITY:
  S_min: PASS
  S_min: FAIL (later contradiction)
  G-completeness: PASS
  d_tool: PASS
  σ_measured: N/A
  q_retest: PASS
NOVELTY:
```
For `S_min`, the first match is `PASS`; `found_pass=True`; loop breaks; later `FAIL` is ignored. Expected admissibility behavior under §15 is to reject contradictory gate evidence or at least not treat the gate as cleanly passing. This silently accepts an internally inconsistent block. VERIFIED: TRUE.

CONFIRM C0016 | Evidence: current code sets `status_pattern = r"(PASS|FAIL|N/A|NA)" if gate == "σ_measured" else r"(PASS|FAIL)"` and treats `σ_measured` status `N/A` or `NA` as pass without checking whether the finding contains a proposed fix. Concrete input:
```text
FIX:
<<<< SEARCH bench/foo.py
old
====
new
>>>> REPLACE

ADMISSIBILITY:
  S_min: PASS
  G-completeness: PASS
  d_tool: PASS
  σ_measured: N/A
  q_retest: PASS
NOVELTY:
```
The parser returns no failure for `σ_measured`, although §15 requires measured pre/post verification when a fix is proposed. VERIFIED: TRUE.

CONFIRM C0028 | Evidence: current marker regex begins after optional hashes with literal `ADMISSIBILITY`, so it does not match Markdown-bold section headers. Concrete input:
```text
**ADMISSIBILITY:**
  S_min: PASS
  G-completeness: PASS
  d_tool: PASS
  σ_measured: N/A
  q_retest: PASS
NOVELTY:
```
At line start the first non-space character is `*`, not `A`; `marker_match` is `None`; function returns all gates failed. This rejects a visually clear admissibility block. VERIFIED: TRUE.

CHALLENGE C0033 | Evidence: C0033 claims returning all five gates for empty `finding_text` is a flaw. The artifact’s own contract states: “If the block is missing entirely, returns all five gates.” Empty input has no `ADMISSIBILITY` marker, so it is a missing-block case. Concrete input `finding_text=""` returns `list(ADMISSIBILITY_GATES)`, which matches the stated function contract and §17 feedback behavior. Falsifier would be a local spec requiring empty input to return `[]` or a distinct error; the supplied artifact states the opposite. VERIFIED: TRUE.

NO_NEW_DISCOVERY_FINDINGS: TRUE

NULL_DISCOVERY_JUSTIFICATION:
I reviewed the remaining high-impact parser surfaces in the supplied artifact: admissibility marker detection, section termination, gate-name matching, status matching, duplicate/contradictory gate handling, missing-block behavior, and `σ_measured` special handling. The high/critical mechanisms I could reproduce are already represented in the registry: unanchored gate/status matching, duplicate-status acceptance, unconditional `σ_measured: N/A`, brittle marker parsing, brittle section terminators, and missing/empty block handling. I did not find a genuinely new CRITICAL or HIGH issue distinct from the active or settled canonical entries. Medium/low cosmetic permissiveness, such as accepting a missing separator between gate name and status, is outside this proof-of-concept review threshold. Final stance: no new discovery finding is filed this round.
